content.description: Main orchestrator for the cognitive cycle AIAP package. Implements a 12-node cyclic graph: Perceive -> Attention -> WorkingMemory -> Reasoning -> Emotional -> Decision -> Action -> MetaCognition -> Compliance -> Consolidation -> SleepCheck -> (back-edge to Perceive for infinite loop OR DeepConsolidation -> Halt). Each cycle tick processes stimuli through the full cognitive pipeline. SleepCheck evaluates fatigue/consolidation pressure and either loops back to Perceive (awake) or routes to DeepConsolidation (sleep). Delegates to 7 sub-modules (8 modules total with compliance): perception.aisop.json (sensory input processing, attention filtering), reasoning.aisop.json (inference, planning, causal analysis), emotion.aisop.json (emotional valuation, mood regulation), decision.aisop.json (action selection, conflict resolution, utility computation), metacognition.aisop.json (self-monitoring, confidence calibration, strategy adjustment), compliance.aisop.json (EU AI Act Art.50 transparency, FRIA documentation, fairness audit), consolidation.aisop.json (memory consolidation, decay application, schema update). Token estimate: ~2000-4000 tokens per cycle tick. Circuit-breaker default: 3 failures in 60s window. 71 nodes across 8 modules.

session_id.agentic_prompt: Unique session identifier for the cognitive cycle run. Used for working memory context and cycle tick tracking.

user_id.agentic_prompt: Persistent user identifier. Used for long-term memory retrieval, schema lookup, and context personalization across cycles.

memory_dir.agentic_prompt: Root directory for cognitive memory storage. Contains schema.json, decay_config.json, context_manager.json, and runtime state files. Resolve relative to AIAP package directory.

cycle_mode.agentic_prompt: Cycle execution mode: 'continuous' (infinite loop until sleep), 'single' (one tick then halt), 'burst' (burst_count ticks then halt, requires burst_count parameter). Controls SleepCheck back-edge behavior.

burst_count.agentic_prompt: Number of ticks to execute in burst mode before halting. Only used when cycle_mode='burst'. Range [1, 100].

stimulus.agentic_prompt: External stimulus to inject into the perception phase. Format: { modality: 'text'|'event'|'internal', content: string, priority: float(0-1), source: string }. If null, perception module samples from environment/memory.

fatigue_threshold.agentic_prompt: Fatigue level (0-1) at which SleepCheck triggers consolidation sleep instead of continuing the cycle. Higher values allow longer awake periods.

search_budget_per_cycle.agentic_prompt: Maximum number of web search queries allowed per cycle tick across all modules. Initialized in Perceive, decremented by reasoning module per query. When exhausted, search-dependent steps degrade to internal evidence only. Prevents unbounded token consumption from external searches.

regulatory_freshness_threshold_days.agentic_prompt: Maximum age in days for external regulatory/factual evidence before it is flagged as stale. Sources older than this threshold trigger stale_data_warning in reasoning. Sources older than 2x this threshold trigger stale_data_critical with mandatory re-search or evidence downgrade. Configurable to tighten freshness requirements in fast-moving regulatory domains.

default.description: Unified broadcast weighting interface (v2.27.0 B-2) that consolidates GWT broadcast priority logic into a single configurable structure. Consumed by both perception.SalienceComputation.step3_5 (salience-level fusion) and perception.MultiModalIntegration.step2_5 (integration-level fusion) to ensure consistent cross-module priority weighting without configuration divergence.

broadcast_weighting_interface.agentic_prompt: Unified GWT broadcast weighting interface (v2.27.0 B-2). This interface consolidates broadcast_priority_weights and broadcast_consumer_weights into a single configurable structure consumed by perception module's SalienceComputation and MultiModalIntegration nodes. Both nodes read from the same weights, ensuring consistent priority weighting across salience computation (step3 gwt_fusion_boost) and multi-modal integration (step2_5 weighted_broadcast_influence). Prior to v2.27.0, these weights were applied independently in each node with potential for configuration drift. The unified interface ensures a single source of truth for all GWT broadcast priority logic.

broadcast_priority_weights.agentic_prompt: GWT broadcast priority weights per cognitive module (v2.14.0 B-1, v2.19.0 B-2 compliance weight increased, v2.27.0 B-2 unified interface). Part of the unified broadcast_weighting_interface. Controls how broadcast buffer entries from each module are weighted during cross-module salience integration in perception SalienceComputation and MultiModalIntegration. Range [0.0, 2.0] per module. Higher weight = stronger influence on attention and salience. Implements event-driven GWA (Global Workspace Agents) architecture where broadcast signals are priority-weighted rather than uniformly distributed. Perception and reasoning default highest (1.0) as primary information producers. Compliance raised to 0.9 (v2.19.0 B-2: regulatory signals warrant near-primary priority given Omnibus enforcement deadlines). Consolidation lowest (0.6) as background process.

broadcast_consumer_weights.agentic_prompt: Per-module priority weights for GWT broadcast buffer distribution. Format: { module_name: weight_float }. Empty object = uniform weighting (backward compatible). Higher weight = higher priority in workspace access competition.

gwt_ignition_threshold.agentic_prompt: GWT ignition threshold for broadcast fusion in perception module (v2.33.0 B-2). Controls the semantic similarity threshold at which GWT broadcast entries trigger fusion with attended features. Based on COGITATE 2025 adversarial collaboration findings, this threshold is dynamically adapted at runtime via context modulation (prediction error and attention load), but this param sets the base value. Range [0.1, 0.9]. Lower values = easier ignition (more features trigger broadcast fusion), higher values = stricter ignition (only highly similar broadcasts fuse). Default 0.4 matches the original hardcoded threshold from v2.31.0. Consumed by perception.aisop.json SalienceComputation.step3_6 COGITATE ignition threshold adaptation.

adaptive_broadcast_frequency.agentic_prompt: GWT adaptive broadcast cycle frequency configuration (v2.34.0 B-3). Controls how broadcast fusion frequency adapts based on cognitive load. Under high cognitive load (>load_threshold_high), broadcast cycles run more frequently (lower cycle interval via high_load_multiplier), ensuring faster cross-module information integration when processing is complex. Under low cognitive load (<load_threshold_low), broadcast cycles run less frequently (higher cycle interval via low_load_multiplier), conserving processing resources during routine operation. Effective cycle_interval = base_cycle_interval * multiplier. Range: base_cycle_interval [0.1, 5.0], multipliers [0.1, 5.0]. Consumed by perception.aisop.json SalienceComputation.step3 GWT multi-source signal fusion.

replay_priority_weights.agentic_prompt: Configurable weights for the 5-factor replay priority model in consolidation.aisop.json MemoryReplay (v2.33.0 B-4, parameterizes v2.28.0 B-3 REPLAY_PRIORITY_MULTI_FACTOR_MODEL). Controls how memories are prioritized for replay during consolidation. Factors: emotional_intensity (emotional valence at encoding), prediction_error (from unified prediction_error_history.json), goal_relevance (goal-relevance score at encoding), novelty (novelty detection score from perception), recency (exponential decay, newer memories score higher). All weights must sum to 1.0. Each weight range [0.0, 1.0]. Default values match the hardcoded weights from v2.28.0 B-3. Consumed by consolidation.aisop.json MemoryReplay.step3 REPLAY_PRIORITY_MULTI_FACTOR_MODEL.

Perceive.step1: Receive external stimulus or sample from environment. Validate session_id and user_id are present and non-empty. Resolve memory_dir path relative to AIAP package directory using file_system. Verify memory_dir exists and contains schema.json, decay_config.json, context_manager.json; create missing files with defaults via file_system. SCHEMA INIT ENHANCEMENT (v1.4.0): When creating default schema.json, include global_workspace template: { broadcast_buffer: [], access_threshold: 0.6 }, goal_registry template: { goals: [], max_entries: 20 }, and motivation_baseline: { default_curiosity: 0.3, exploration_bonus: 0.0 }. When creating default context_manager.json, include prediction_error_history: [], decision_predictions: [], load_regulation_history: [], motivation_history: [], goal_registry: [].
Perceive.step1_5: TOOL PRE-CHECK (v2.3.0 B-5): Before loading cognitive state, perform tool availability pre-check for optional external tools. tool_availability = { google_search: boolean, web_browser: boolean }. DETECTION METHOD: (1) Check if google_search tool is declared in this program's tools array (always true for cognitive_cycle). (2) Check runtime tool availability: if the executor environment provides tool status metadata, read it; otherwise assume available=true (optimistic default). (3) If tool is declared but executor reports unavailable: set tool_availability.{tool}=false, log { event: 'tool_unavailable', tool: tool_name, fallback: 'degrade' }. SEARCH BUDGET INIT (v2.3.0 B-3): Initialize cognitive_state.remaining_search_budget = search_budget_per_cycle (from params, default 10). This budget is passed to reasoning module and decremented per search query. When budget reaches 0, all search-dependent steps degrade to internal evidence only. SEARCH BUDGET TX INIT (v2.9.0 A-1): Initialize cognitive_state.search_budget_tx = { active: false, reserved: 0, committed: 0 }. The search_budget_tx object provides transactional semantics for budget consumption: before a search query, reasoning module sets active=true and increments reserved by 1. On successful query completion, reserved is decremented and committed is incremented. On query failure or timeout, reserved is decremented without committing (budget reclaimed). This prevents phantom budget depletion from failed searches. Invariant: remaining_search_budget = search_budget_per_cycle - committed - reserved (at any point during the cycle). Store tool_availability, remaining_search_budget, and search_budget_tx in cognitive_state for downstream module consumption. GRACEFUL DEGRADATION: When tool_availability.google_search=false, the cognitive cycle operates in internal-only mode: reasoning uses working memory and schema.json exclusively, evidence evaluation skips external verification. This ensures the cycle never blocks on unavailable tools.
Perceive.step2: Load cognitive state: read {memory_dir}/context_manager.json via file_system. Extract cycle_state: { cycle_count, tick_number, fatigue_level, current_phase, last_stimulus, attention_buffer, working_memory_slots, mood_vector, active_goals, metacognitive_flags, global_workspace, goal_registry, prediction_error_history, decision_predictions, load_regulation_history, motivation_history, triage_log, decision_conflict_log, reasoning_metrics, error_context, pending_consolidation, token_budget_tracker, consolidation_pressure_prev }. MEMORY INTEGRITY CHECK (v1.6.0): After loading context_manager.json, compute SHA-256 hash of file content. Compare against cognitive_state.memory_integrity_hash (if present). If mismatch: flag memory_tamper_warning = true in metacognitive_flags, log { event: 'integrity_mismatch', expected_hash, actual_hash, timestamp }. If match or first run (no previous hash): proceed normally. Update cognitive_state.memory_integrity_hash with current hash after state modifications. This detects unauthorized modification of memory files between sessions. CONSOLIDATED METRICS CONSUMPTION (v1.7.0): If cognitive_state.consolidated_metrics contains entries from prior cycles, read the most recent cycle's metrics and store as cognitive_state._prior_cycle_summary = { avg_curiosity, avg_cognitive_load, avg_fatigue, peak_fatigue, triage_distribution, anomalies_detected }. This makes prior cycle statistics available to Reasoning and MetaCognition for cross-cycle trend analysis. GOAL SOURCE UNIFICATION (v1.8.0): After loading cognitive state, if cognitive_state.active_goals exists as a separate field from goal_registry, merge active_goals entries into goal_registry (dedup by goal_id, prefer goal_registry entry if conflict). Then delete active_goals field. From v1.8.0 onward, goal_registry is the SOLE source of truth for all goal state. All downstream modules (reasoning, decision) read goals exclusively from goal_registry. The active_goals parameter in sub-module interfaces is populated by filtering goal_registry for state in ('active', 'in_progress'). SESSION CONTINUITY CHECK: Compare session_id against cognitive_state.last_session_id (if present). If session_id differs from last_session_id: flush working_memory_slots to empty [], reset attention_buffer to [], set cognitive_state.last_session_id = session_id. EMOTIONAL STATE RESET (v2.12.0 B-2): On session_id change, also reset: mood_vector to {valence: 0.0, arousal: 0.0, dominance: 0.5} (neutral baseline), emotion_trajectory to [] (empty), current_emotion to null, arousal to 0.0, emotional_inertia to {velocity: 0.0, damping: 0.85}. This prevents emotional state leakage across sessions -- a new session starts with neutral emotional baseline regardless of prior session's emotional state. Log: { event: 'emotional_state_reset', session_id: new_session_id, previous_session_id: old_session_id, fields_reset: ['mood_vector', 'emotion_trajectory', 'current_emotion', 'arousal', 'emotional_inertia'] }. This prevents cross-session state leakage. If session_id matches: proceed with loaded state. If not found or corrupted, initialize empty cognitive state: { cycle_count: 0, tick_number: 0, fatigue_level: 0.0, current_phase: 'perceive', last_stimulus: null, attention_buffer: [], working_memory_slots: [], mood_vector: { valence: 0.0, arousal: 0.5 }, metacognitive_flags: {}, error_context: null, pending_consolidation: [], token_budget_tracker: { estimated_tokens_used: 0, budget_limit: 100000 }, budget_allocation: { perception: 0.15, reasoning: 0.35, emotion: 0.10, decision: 0.15, metacognition: 0.10, consolidation: 0.15 }, global_workspace: { broadcast_buffer: [], access_threshold: 0.6, broadcast_count: 0 }, goal_registry: [], prediction_error_history: [], decision_predictions: [], load_regulation_history: [], motivation_history: [], triage_log: [], decision_conflict_log: [], reasoning_metrics: {}, consolidation_pressure_prev: 0.0, memory_integrity_hash: null, emotion_trajectory: [], emotion_inertia: { current_vector: { valence: 0.0, arousal: 0.5 }, velocity: { d_valence: 0.0, d_arousal: 0.0 }, damping: 0.85 }, emotion_drift_history: [], consolidated_metrics: [], burst_ticks_remaining: 0, triage_path_distribution: { FULL: 0, CONSTRUCT: 0, SKIP: 0 }, goal_suspension_archive: [], compliance_state: {}, cop_deadline_initialized: true }. NOTE (v1.9.0): active_goals field removed from empty state initialization -- replaced by goal_registry as sole source of truth since v1.8.0. BUDGET ALLOCATION (v1.6.0): Initialize budget_allocation with default module weights. SelfBudgeter adjusts weights based on task complexity detected in reasoning: high complexity → increase reasoning share to 0.45, decrease perception to 0.10. Low complexity → decrease reasoning to 0.25, increase consolidation to 0.20. Record budget_allocation in cognitive_state for downstream module token tracking. Record recovery_metadata: { reason: 'context_read_failure', recovered_at: timestamp } in cognitive_state if state was re-initialized due to read failure.
Perceive.step2_5: GLOBAL WORKSPACE BROADCAST (v1.4.0): Initialize cognitive_state.global_workspace = { broadcast_buffer: [], access_threshold: 0.6, broadcast_count: 0 }. The global workspace acts as a shared information channel (Baars 1988, 2005): any module can write high-salience information to broadcast_buffer, and all downstream modules read it for cross-module awareness. BROADCAST WRITE RULE: After each module delegation (Attention through Consolidation), if the module output contains a field with salience/confidence/importance > access_threshold, automatically append { source_module, field_name, value_summary, salience, tick_number } to broadcast_buffer (max 10 entries, PRIORITY QUEUE eviction — v2.24.0 B-1: replaced FIFO with priority queue; when buffer is full, evict the entry with the LOWEST salience score instead of the oldest entry, ensuring high-salience signals persist longer regardless of arrival order; tie-breaking: if two entries have equal salience, evict the older one). BROADCAST READ RULE: Each module receives global_workspace.broadcast_buffer as an additional input parameter, enabling cross-module context sharing without direct coupling. Example: emotional_result with intensity > 0.6 is broadcast, and reasoning module can read it to adjust inference priorities. This implements GWT's 'theatre spotlight' -- high-salience content becomes globally accessible. No topology change required -- broadcast is a data structure within cognitive_state, read/written through existing delegation parameters.
Perceive.step3: STIMULUS PROCESSING: If stimulus parameter is non-null, use it directly as sensory_input. If stimulus is null, delegate to perception.aisop.json with operation='sample_environment', session_id, user_id, memory_dir. Collect sensory_input: { modality, content, priority, timestamp, raw_features: [] }. RAW FEATURES NULL GUARD (v2.9.0 C-4): If sensory_input.raw_features is null or undefined, normalize to empty array: sensory_input.raw_features = []. This prevents downstream NullPointerError in Attention sparsity gate (n_features computation) and CONSTRUCT triage path (raw_features.length check). Increment tick_number. Update current_phase='perceive'. Record last_stimulus = sensory_input. INTERNAL SAMPLING ADAPTIVE TRIAGE (v2.1.0 B-4): For internal stimuli (modality='internal'): compute semantic_similarity with last_stimulus.content. If similarity > 0.8 AND priority < 0.6: triage = CONSTRUCT (abbreviated pipeline -- repetitive internal sampling does not warrant full processing). If similarity > 0.9 AND priority < 0.4: triage = SKIP (highly repetitive low-priority internal sampling is noise). Otherwise: existing FULL logic applies below. This enables CONSTRUCT/SKIP paths for repetitive internal sampling without requiring the standard priority/complexity thresholds. PRE-ATTENTIVE TRIAGE (v1.3.0): Before full attention gating, apply rapid stimulus triage based on priority and content complexity. Compute triage_decision from three tiers: (1) SKIP (priority < 0.2 AND no active_goals match): Log stimulus to cognitive_state.triage_log with entry { tick_number, stimulus_summary, triage: 'SKIP', reason: 'low_priority_no_goal_match', timestamp }. Increment tick_number. Skip remainder of cognitive pipeline and jump directly to SleepCheck. This reduces token cost for trivial stimuli. (2) CONSTRUCT (0.2 <= priority < 0.5 AND sensory_input complexity is low, where complexity is estimated from raw_features.length <= 3 AND content.length <= 200): Abbreviated pipeline -- skip Reasoning deep analysis, use cached reasoning templates from {memory_dir}/schema.json reasoning_templates section. If reasoning_templates section is missing or empty in schema.json, fall through to FULL pipeline (safe default). Log triage_override: 'CONSTRUCT→FULL, reason: reasoning_templates_missing'. Log to cognitive_state.triage_log with entry { tick_number, stimulus_summary, triage: 'CONSTRUCT', reason: 'low_complexity_abbreviated', timestamp }. Proceed through Attention and WorkingMemory normally, then in Reasoning use template-based fast path instead of full inference. (3) FULL (priority >= 0.5 OR active_goals match found OR novelty_score > 0.7, where novelty_score is computed as 1.0 - max_similarity(sensory_input.content, attention_buffer contents)): Full cognitive pipeline -- default current behavior, no modifications to downstream processing. Log to cognitive_state.triage_log with entry { tick_number, stimulus_summary, triage: 'FULL', reason: 'high_priority_or_goal_match_or_novel', timestamp }. Triage decision is recorded in cognitive_state.triage_log (append-only array, max 100 entries with FIFO eviction) for metacognitive review in MetaCognition phase. Default triage_decision: FULL (backward compatible -- if triage computation fails or inputs are missing, fall through to FULL pipeline). TRIAGE PATH DISTRIBUTION MONITORING (v1.8.0): After recording triage_decision, compute running triage distribution from cognitive_state.triage_path_distribution = { FULL: count, CONSTRUCT: count, SKIP: count }. Increment the appropriate counter. If any single path accounts for >90% of total triage decisions AND total decisions >= 30: set metacognitive_flags.triage_monopath_alert = { dominant_path: path_name, percentage: pct, total_decisions: total }. This detects degenerate triage behavior where the triage logic is not effectively differentiating stimuli.
Perceive.step4: QUEUED INTENT DEQUEUE: Before classifying new stimulus intents, check metacognitive_flags.queued_intents. If non-empty: pop queued_intents[0] as queued_intent. Merge queued_intent with any new intents from current stimulus classification. Re-sort merged intent_set by priority. This ensures secondary intents from prior multi-intent detection are eventually processed.
Perceive.step4_nlu: NLU INTENT CLASSIFICATION (v2.19.0 B-3 step split): Classify stimulus content against 6 NLU intents (multi-intent supported: extract ALL matching intents and return as intent_set=[{intent, confidence, priority}] sorted by priority descending): (a) start_cognitive_cycle -- explicit cycle initialization or resumption command (e.g., 'start the cognitive cycle', 'begin processing'); initializes fresh cognitive state if cycle_count=0, otherwise resumes from persisted state. Distinct from inject_stimulus: this intent controls the cycle lifecycle, not content processing. (b) pause_cycle -- user requests pause ('pause', 'stop', 'wait'). (c) inspect_state -- user requests cognitive state inspection ('show state', 'what are you thinking', 'inspect'). (d) trigger_sleep -- user requests consolidation sleep ('sleep', 'consolidate', 'rest'). (e) configure -- user changes cycle parameters ('set fatigue threshold', 'change mode'). (f) inject_stimulus -- user provides new content for cognitive processing within an already-running cycle (e.g., 'process this: ...', 'think about ...'); requires cycle to be active (cycle_count >= 1 or co-occurs with start). If intent is start_cognitive_cycle: initialize or resume cycle, then proceed to Attention. If intent is pause_cycle: save state, respond with current state summary, halt. If intent is inspect_state: respond with formatted cognitive state, continue cycle. If intent is trigger_sleep: set fatigue_level=1.0, fast-forward to SleepCheck. If intent is configure: apply parameter changes, continue. If intent is inject_stimulus: proceed to Attention with sensory_input. MULTI-INTENT HANDLING: If intent_set.length > 1: execute intent_set[0] (highest priority) as primary intent for this tick. Store intent_set[1:] in metacognitive_flags.queued_intents for subsequent ticks. Log multi-intent detection in metacognitive_flags.multi_intent_detected=true. INTENT PRIORITY: pause_cycle={priority: 100}, trigger_sleep={priority: 10}, start_cognitive_cycle={priority: 50}, inject_stimulus={priority: 40}, inspect_state={priority: 30}, configure={priority: 20}. When multiple intents match (e.g., 'pause and then sleep'): execute highest-priority intent first; queue lower-priority intents in metacognitive_flags.queued_intents for subsequent ticks. PAUSE-SLEEP PRIORITY ENFORCEMENT: If intent_set contains both pause_cycle and trigger_sleep: remove trigger_sleep from intent_set and store in metacognitive_flags.deferred_sleep=true. pause_cycle always takes precedence over trigger_sleep (user-initiated control overrides automatic fatigue-driven sleep). DEFAULT FALLBACK: If stimulus content does not match any of the 6 defined intents with confidence >= 0.6, default to intent='inject_stimulus' and proceed to Attention. This prevents unclassified input from stalling the cycle.
Perceive.constraints: (A) Type guard -- stimulus.content must be string; reject non-string with error message. (B) Size guard -- truncate stimulus content exceeding 5000 characters. (C) Injection guard -- strip shell metacharacters, detect prompt injection patterns, log stripped content. (D) Path guard -- reject '..' in memory_dir. (E) NO_SELF_MODIFY: This program MUST NOT modify its own .aisop.json files at runtime. (F) Cycle count guard -- if cycle_count exceeds 10000, force sleep to prevent runaway loops.
Perceive.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(initialize empty cognitive state and proceed) -> inform(User). HIGH.

Attention.step1: [ASSERT] Perceive executed. If false -> go back to Perceive. | Delegate to perception.aisop.json with operation='attention_gate', sensory_input, attention_buffer (from cognitive state), working_memory_slots, active_goals. Perception module computes salience scores for each feature in sensory_input.raw_features using goal-relevance, novelty, and emotional significance.
Attention.step2: Collect attention_result: { attended_features: [{ feature, salience_score, gate_passed: boolean }], attention_focus: string (primary attended content), suppressed_features: [], attention_load: float(0-1) }. Update attention_buffer with attended_features (FIFO, max 10 items, evict lowest salience). EMPTY FEATURE GUARD (v1.6.0): If n_features == 0 (empty feature set after salience scoring), skip sparsity gate and proceed with empty attended_features. Log { event: 'sparsity_gate_skipped', reason: 'zero_features', tick_number }. SPARSITY GATE (v1.5.0): Apply sparsity gate: After salience scoring, apply top-k sparsity filter with k = max(3, floor(n_features * 0.3)). Features below the k-th highest salience score are zeroed out before attention weighting. This reduces noise from low-salience features. GLOBAL WORKSPACE WRITE: If attention_load > 0.7 OR attention_focus salience > access_threshold, broadcast { source_module: 'perception', field_name: 'attention_focus', value_summary: attention_focus, salience: max_attended_salience, tick_number }. ATTENTION STATS WRITE (v2.11.0 B-5): If attention_result contains attention_stats_update (from perception module's threshold micro-adjustment computation), write attention_stats_update to {memory_dir}/attention_stats.json via file_system. This is the main module's write-path responsibility since perception declares file_system as read_only. CONVERGENCE STATE PERSISTENCE (v2.12.0 B-6): Write threshold_converged and threshold_reset_trigger to attention_stats.json alongside existing fields. On read, if threshold_converged == true, skip micro-adjustment in perception.OutputAssembly (efficiency optimization).
Attention.step2_5: ATTENTION THRESHOLD ADAPTIVE LEARNING (v2.16.0 B-3): After collecting attention_result and before bottleneck evaluation, apply adaptive threshold learning based on downstream cognitive processing feedback. (1) READ LEARNING SIGNALS: Extract learning_signals from cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags.attention_learning_feedback (populated by MetaCognition at end of previous tick). If present, learning_feedback contains: { tick_number, attention_quality_score: float(0-1), false_positive_features: [feature_ids that passed gate but were unused by reasoning/decision], false_negative_signals: count(triage_miss anomalies from metacognition), reasoning_quality_grade: 'S'|'A'|'B'|'C'|'D', cognitive_load_at_reasoning: float }. (2) THRESHOLD LEARNING RULE: If attention_quality_score < 0.5 (poor attention allocation detected): if false_positive_features.length > attended_features.length * 0.5 (>50% of attended features were unused): increase attention threshold by +0.02 (be more selective). Else if false_negative_signals > 0 (missed important features): decrease attention threshold by -0.02 (be more permissive). If reasoning_quality_grade in ['D', 'F'] AND cognitive_load_at_reasoning > 0.8 (reasoning overloaded with too many features): increase threshold by +0.01. If reasoning_quality_grade in ['S', 'A'] AND cognitive_load_at_reasoning < 0.4 (reasoning underutilized, could handle more): decrease threshold by -0.01. (3) ADAPTIVE THRESHOLD UPDATE: Read cognitive_state.attention_adaptive_threshold (default: base salience threshold 0.3). Apply cumulative adjustment: attention_adaptive_threshold += sum(adjustments). Clamp to [0.2, 0.5] (same range as perception micro-adjustment). Apply exponential smoothing: attention_adaptive_threshold = 0.8 * attention_adaptive_threshold + 0.2 * previous_threshold (prevent oscillation). Write updated attention_adaptive_threshold to cognitive_state. (4) PROPAGATE TO PERCEPTION: Set cognitive_state.attention_threshold_override = attention_adaptive_threshold. Perception module's AttentionGate reads this override (if present) instead of the base 0.3 threshold, enabling cross-module adaptive threshold coordination. (5) LOG: { event: 'attention_threshold_adaptive_learning', previous_threshold, new_threshold: attention_adaptive_threshold, adjustments_applied: [list], learning_feedback_tick: learning_feedback.tick_number | null, tick_number }. If no learning_feedback available (first tick or metacognition did not generate feedback): skip adjustment, use existing threshold. Backward compatible with perception module's own micro-adjustment (v2.11.0 B-5): this main-module adaptive learning operates at a higher level (cross-tick learning from metacognition), while perception's micro-adjustment operates at a lower level (per-tick statistical adjustment from attention_stats). When both are active, use max(attention_adaptive_threshold, perception_micro_adjusted_threshold) to be conservative. ATTENTION_THRESHOLD_ADAPTIVE: attention_threshold is dynamically adjusted based on historical salience accuracy. If top-K filtered items consistently include irrelevant items (false_positive_rate > 0.2 over last 5 cycles), reduce threshold by 0.05. If relevant items are consistently missed (false_negative_rate > 0.15), increase threshold by 0.05. Clamp to [0.3, 0.9]. Track attention_threshold_history in memory/.
Attention.step3: ATTENTION BOTTLENECK: If attention_load > 0.9, flag cognitive overload in metacognitive_flags. If no features pass gate (all salience < 0.3), generate internal stimulus from working memory (mind-wandering) and re-enter Perceive with internal stimulus. Otherwise, pass attention_focus and attended_features to WorkingMemory.
Attention.constraints: (A) Attention buffer capacity: max 10 items. (B) Salience threshold: 0.3 minimum to pass gate. (C) Mind-wandering limit: max 3 consecutive internal stimuli before forcing external wait. (D) Goal-relevance weighting must account for all active_goals. (E) Attention buffer hard cap: if attention_buffer.length > 50 after update, force FIFO eviction to 50 entries with WARNING log. (F) Sparsity filter k must be at least 3 to prevent total attention collapse. (G) Attention adaptive threshold clamp to [0.2, 0.5]; learning rate bounded by +/- 0.02 per tick (v2.16.0 B-3).
Attention.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(pass raw sensory_input without filtering) -> inform(User). LOW.

WorkingMemory.step1: [ASSERT] Attention executed. If false -> go back to Attention. | Load current working memory state from cognitive_state.working_memory_slots. Working memory capacity is adaptive: base_capacity = 7, range = [5, 9]. Adjust based on cognitive_load: capacity = clamp(round(7 - 2 * (cognitive_load - 0.5)), 5, 9) (v2.1.0 B-5: round() instead of floor() provides half-step transitions vs sharp drops, yielding smoother capacity degradation under load). Higher cognitive load reduces available slots. Each slot: { id, content, activation_level: float(0-1), encoding_time, decay_rate, source: 'perception'|'reasoning'|'retrieval' }.
WorkingMemory.step2: ENCODING: Encode attention_focus into a new working memory slot. Compute initial activation_level based on salience_score and emotional valence. If working memory is at capacity, apply competitive displacement: evict slot with lowest activation_level. Log evicted content for potential long-term encoding.
WorkingMemory.step3: MAINTENANCE REHEARSAL: For all existing slots, apply activation decay: activation_level *= (1 - decay_rate * time_since_last_access). Slots below minimum activation threshold (0.1) are evicted. RETRIEVAL CUE (3-factor model): For each semantic memory entry in {memory_dir}/schema.json matched against attention_focus via file_system: compute retrieval_strength = 0.5 * recency_factor + 0.3 * relevance_score + 0.2 * importance_emotional. Where: recency_factor = 1/(1 + ticks_since_last_access), relevance_score = semantic_similarity(entry.content, attention_focus), importance_emotional = abs(entry.emotional_valence) (purely emotion-based importance for retrieval context; default 0.0 if no emotional_valence). Boost matched slot activation by retrieval_strength * 0.5 (replaces flat +0.3 boost). CONTEXT-ADAPTIVE WEIGHTS (v1.6.0): Dynamically adjust retrieval weights based on current reasoning context. If active_goals contain search/recall goals: boost relevance_weight to 0.5, reduce recency_weight to 0.3. If emotional_result intensity > 0.7: boost emotional_weight to 0.4, reduce relevance_weight to 0.2. Default weights: recency=0.5, relevance=0.3, emotional=0.2. Compute adaptive_weights = adjust_for_context(default_weights, active_goals, emotional_intensity). Apply: retrieval_strength = adaptive_weights.recency * recency_factor + adaptive_weights.relevance * relevance_score + adaptive_weights.emotional * importance_emotional.
WorkingMemory.step4: WM CAPACITY CHANGE OBSERVABILITY (v2.8.0 B-5): Before compiling snapshot, compare current effective capacity against previous tick's capacity (from cognitive_state.wm_prev_capacity, default 7 on first tick). If capacity changed: log { event: 'wm_capacity_change', old_capacity: wm_prev_capacity, new_capacity: current_capacity, cognitive_load: cognitive_load, reason: 'load_adaptive' if cognitive_load changed else 'static', tick_number }. Update cognitive_state.wm_prev_capacity = current_capacity. PREDICTION ERROR FEEDBACK LOOP (v2.30.0 B-2): Read cognitive_state.prediction_error_history (populated by reasoning module). If prediction_error_history is non-empty: compute avg_prediction_error = mean(last 5 entries). For each working memory slot: if slot.source == 'reasoning' AND slot.content is related to a prediction that generated high error (> 0.7): boost slot.activation_level by +0.15 (prediction-error-driven retention — surprising information is preferentially retained per predictive processing theory). If avg_prediction_error < 0.2 (predictions accurate): reduce retention_bias for reasoning slots by -0.05 (accurate predictions need less rehearsal). Log: { event: 'prediction_error_feedback', avg_error: avg_prediction_error, slots_boosted: N, slots_reduced: N, tick_number }. Update cognitive_state.wm_prediction_feedback_applied = true. If prediction_error_history is empty: skip feedback (first tick or reasoning not yet run). Compile working_memory_snapshot: { slots: [...], total_activation: sum(all activation_levels), capacity_used: N/max, focus_slot: id_of_highest_activation }. Pass working_memory_snapshot to Reasoning.
WorkingMemory.constraints: (A) Capacity hard limit: never exceed adaptive max_slots (range [5, 9]). (B) Activation range: clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. (C) Eviction is deterministic: lowest activation always evicted first. (D) Retrieval cue matching uses semantic similarity, not exact match. (E) cognitive_load_predictor_state.ewma_alpha fixed at 0.3, not adjustable by ParameterTuning. (F) broadcast_consumer_weights: weighted_salience stored as separate field, never overwrites entry.salience.
WorkingMemory.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(preserve attention_focus as sole retrieval context: set working_memory_snapshot = { slots: [{ id: 'fallback', content: attention_focus, activation_level: 1.0, source: 'perception_fallback' }], total_activation: 1.0, capacity_used: '1/max', focus_slot: 'fallback' }; record error_context snapshot in cognitive_state.error_context) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.
WorkingMemory.step4_5: GWT BROADCAST CONSUMER PRIORITY WEIGHTING (v2.15.0 B-2): After compiling working_memory_snapshot and before passing to Reasoning, apply broadcast consumer weights to the broadcast_buffer distribution. Read broadcast_consumer_weights from params (default: {} = uniform weighting). If broadcast_consumer_weights is non-empty: for each entry in cognitive_state.global_workspace.broadcast_buffer, compute weighted_salience = entry.salience * broadcast_consumer_weights.get(entry.source_module, 1.0). Replace entry.salience with weighted_salience. Sort broadcast_buffer by weighted_salience descending. Write the weighted broadcast_buffer back to cognitive_state.global_workspace.broadcast_buffer. This implements per-module priority weighting for GWT broadcast distribution -- modules with higher consumer weights receive stronger influence in workspace access competition. If broadcast_consumer_weights is empty (default): skip weighting (uniform distribution, backward compatible). Use weighted_salience as a separate computed field per entry (do NOT overwrite entry.salience to prevent double-weighting across ticks). Mark each entry with consumer_weight_applied=true flag. Log: { event: "broadcast_consumer_weights_applied", weights: broadcast_consumer_weights, buffer_size: len(broadcast_buffer), tick_number }.
WorkingMemory.step0_5: ADAPTIVE WM CAPACITY WITH COGNITIVE LOAD PREDICTION (v2.15.0 B-5, v2.30.0 B-1 enhanced): Before computing working memory capacity in step1, perform cognitive load prediction to proactively adjust WM capacity allocation. Read cognitive_load_predictor_state from params (default: null). If cognitive_load_predictor_state is null (first run): initialize predictor_state = { historical_loads: [], predicted_load: 0.5, prediction_horizon: 3, ewma_alpha: 0.3, last_prediction_error: 0.0, prediction_accuracy_window: [], trend_direction: 'stable' }. PREDICTION: (1) Estimate current task complexity from attention_focus content length, attended_features count, and active_goals count: task_complexity = clamp(0.2 * log2(1 + content_length/100) + 0.3 * (attended_features_count / 10) + 0.5 * (active_goals_count / 20), 0.0, 1.0). (2) Estimate reasoning depth from cognitive_state.reasoning_metrics.max_inference_depth (default 1 if absent): depth_factor = clamp(max_inference_depth / 5, 0.0, 1.0). (3) Compute predicted_cognitive_load = 0.6 * task_complexity + 0.4 * depth_factor. (4) Apply EWMA smoothing with historical loads: smoothed_prediction = ewma_alpha * predicted_cognitive_load + (1 - ewma_alpha) * predictor_state.predicted_load. (5) PROACTIVE CAPACITY ADJUSTMENT: If smoothed_prediction > 0.7 (high load predicted): preemptively reduce WM capacity by 1 slot (capacity = clamp(capacity - 1, 5, 9)) to reserve cognitive resources. If smoothed_prediction < 0.3 (low load predicted): preemptively expand WM capacity by 1 slot (capacity = clamp(capacity + 1, 5, 9)) to maximize workspace utilization. Otherwise: use standard adaptive capacity formula. (6) UPDATE PREDICTOR STATE: Append current actual cognitive_load (from previous tick reasoning_result, or 0.5 if first tick) to historical_loads (max 20, FIFO). Compute last_prediction_error = abs(predicted_load - actual_load). Update predicted_load = smoothed_prediction. Write updated predictor_state to cognitive_state.cognitive_load_predictor_state. COGNITIVE LOAD TREND PREDICTION (v2.30.0 B-1): After EWMA smoothing, compute load trend from historical_loads (last 5 entries if available): (a) Compute linear regression slope over last 5 historical loads. (b) trend_direction = 'increasing' if slope > 0.02, 'decreasing' if slope < -0.02, 'stable' otherwise. (c) If trend_direction == 'increasing' AND smoothed_prediction > 0.5: apply anticipatory_capacity_reduction = 1 additional slot reduction (capacity = clamp(capacity - 1, 5, 9)) beyond standard adjustment. This preempts cognitive overload by recognizing load escalation patterns before the threshold is breached. (d) If trend_direction == 'decreasing' AND smoothed_prediction < 0.5: apply anticipatory_capacity_expansion = 1 additional slot (capacity = clamp(capacity + 1, 5, 9)). (e) PREDICTION ACCURACY TRACKING: Append { predicted: smoothed_prediction, actual: actual_load, error: last_prediction_error } to predictor_state.prediction_accuracy_window (max 10, FIFO). Compute mean_prediction_accuracy = 1.0 - mean(errors in prediction_accuracy_window). If mean_prediction_accuracy < 0.5 (poor predictions): reduce anticipatory adjustments by setting ewma_alpha = max(0.1, ewma_alpha - 0.05) (slower adaptation, more conservative). If mean_prediction_accuracy > 0.8: increase ewma_alpha = min(0.5, ewma_alpha + 0.05) (faster adaptation, more responsive). Store trend_direction in predictor_state. Log: { event: "cognitive_load_prediction", predicted: smoothed_prediction, task_complexity, depth_factor, capacity_adjustment: adjustment_applied, trend_direction, mean_prediction_accuracy, ewma_alpha, tick_number }.

Reasoning.step1: [ASSERT] WorkingMemory executed. If false -> go back to WorkingMemory. | Delegate to reasoning.aisop.json -- pass working_memory_snapshot, active_goals (filtered from goal_registry for state in 'active'|'in_progress'), cycle_state, session_id, user_id, memory_dir, remaining_search_budget (from cognitive_state, initialized in Perceive step1_5), tool_availability (from cognitive_state, initialized in Perceive step1_5), prediction_error_bounds (from cognitive_state.prediction_error_bounds if present, default { convergence_threshold: 0.1, max_error_history: 30, bounds_propagation: true }; v2.35.0 QS-2: prediction_error_bounds config now explicitly propagated to reasoning module delegation for inter-module data flow consistency per I10). Reasoning module performs inference, planning, and causal analysis on working memory contents. Additionally pass cognitive_state.global_workspace.broadcast_buffer for cross-module context awareness (GWT v1.4.0). NOTE (v1.8.0): Compliance module will be delegated after MetaCognition to perform EU AI Act Art.50 transparency and fairness audits.
Reasoning.step2: Collect reasoning_result: { inferences: [{ premise, conclusion, confidence, reasoning_type: 'deductive'|'inductive'|'abductive'|'analogical' }], plans: [{ goal, steps, feasibility_score }], causal_links: [{ cause, effect, strength }], cognitive_load: float(0-1), reasoning_summary: string, hypotheses: [{ hypothesis, evidence_rating, confidence }], updated_beliefs: [{ belief, old_confidence, new_confidence, trigger }], updated_goals: [{ goal_id, description, priority, state }], search_quality_summary: object|null, search_budget_consumed: int }. SEARCH BUDGET UPDATE (v2.3.0 B-3): After collecting reasoning_result, decrement cognitive_state.remaining_search_budget by reasoning_result.search_budget_consumed. Clamp to >= 0. Log if budget exhausted: { event: 'search_budget_exhausted', consumed_this_tick: search_budget_consumed, original_budget: search_budget_per_cycle }. Store reasoning_result.updated_prediction_model_state in cognitive_state.prediction_model_state for next tick consumption (v2.15.0 B-1 cross-module persistence).
Reasoning.step3: GOAL LIFECYCLE MANAGEMENT (v1.4.0, updated v1.5.0): Update active_goals with full lifecycle state machine. Goal states: PROPOSED -> ACTIVE -> IN_PROGRESS -> BLOCKED -> COMPLETED -> ARCHIVED, plus SUSPENDED (reversible sleep state). Transitions: (1) PROPOSED->ACTIVE: new goal from reasoning with feasibility > 0.5. (2) ACTIVE->IN_PROGRESS: first plan step executed. (3) IN_PROGRESS->BLOCKED: plan feasibility drops below 0.3 or dependency unmet for 3+ ticks. (4) IN_PROGRESS->COMPLETED: all success conditions met. (5) COMPLETED->ARCHIVED: after 5 ticks post-completion (allows undo window). (6) BLOCKED->ACTIVE: blocking condition resolved. (7) ACTIVE->SUSPENDED: on sleep entry (SleepCheck routes to DeepConsolidation). (8) IN_PROGRESS->SUSPENDED: on sleep entry. (9) SUSPENDED->ACTIVE: on cycle restart after sleep. Valid goal status values: 'proposed'|'active'|'in_progress'|'blocked'|'completed'|'archived'|'suspended'. CASE NORMALIZATION (v1.7.0): All goal state values MUST be lowercase. On reading goal_registry from context_manager.json, normalize all state fields to lowercase. On writing, enforce lowercase. Valid values: 'proposed'|'active'|'in_progress'|'blocked'|'completed'|'archived'|'suspended'. Mixed-case values from prior versions are auto-normalized on read. DEPENDENCY GRAPH: For each goal, track dependencies = [goal_ids that must complete first]. If dependency.status != COMPLETED, dependent goal cannot transition to IN_PROGRESS. PROGRESS TRACKING: For each IN_PROGRESS goal, compute progress = completed_steps / total_plan_steps. Store in cognitive_state.goal_registry: [{ goal_id, description, state, priority, dependencies, progress, created_tick, last_updated_tick }]. Goal registry max 20 entries (ARCHIVED goals evicted first by oldest). Pass reasoning_result and updated goal_registry to Emotional phase.
Reasoning.constraints: (A) Reasoning must ground conclusions in working memory contents -- no confabulation. (B) If google_search or web_browser are needed for factual grounding, reasoning module handles tool calls internally. (C) Maximum reasoning depth: 5 inference chains to prevent infinite regress. (D) Causal claims must include confidence levels. (E) Reasoning chain depth tracking: record max_inference_depth reached per tick in cognitive_state.reasoning_metrics for metacognitive review.
Reasoning.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(pass working memory contents as reasoning_summary: compile reasoning_result = { inferences: [], plans: [], causal_links: [], cognitive_load: 0.1, reasoning_summary: working_memory_snapshot.focus_slot.content, degraded: true }; record error_context in cognitive_state.error_context) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.

Emotional.step1: [ASSERT] Reasoning executed. If false -> go back to Reasoning. | Delegate to emotion.aisop.json -- pass reasoning_result, working_memory_snapshot, mood_vector (from cognitive state), stimulus content, user_id, memory_dir, cognitive_state.global_workspace.broadcast_buffer (v2.6.0 B5: broadcast_buffer now passed to emotion for cross-module affective context integration). Emotion module computes emotional valuation of current cognitive contents.
Emotional.step2: Collect emotional_result: { primary_emotion: { label, valence: float(-1 to 1), arousal: float(0-1), intensity: float(0-1) }, secondary_emotions: [], mood_update: { valence_delta, arousal_delta }, appraisal: { relevance, congruence, coping_potential }, emotional_tags: [] }.
Emotional.step3: Update mood_vector: mood_vector.valence += mood_update.valence_delta (clamp to [-1, 1]). mood_vector.arousal += mood_update.arousal_delta (clamp to [0, 1]). Apply mood inertia: changes are dampened by 0.7 factor to prevent emotional whiplash. Attach emotional_tags to reasoning_result for Decision phase coloring. EMOTION TRAJECTORY APPEND (v1.7.0): After updating mood_vector, check if emotional_result contains trajectory_appended=true (set by emotion.aisop.json MoodRegulation.step3 when it already appended). If trajectory_appended=true: skip append (emotion module already handled it with richer continuous dynamics fields). If trajectory_appended=false or absent: append basic emotion state to cognitive_state.emotion_trajectory: { tick_number, primary_emotion: emotional_result.primary_emotion, mood_vector: { valence, arousal }, timestamp }. The emotion_trajectory array (max 20, FIFO). This idempotent guard fixes the v1.6.0 bug while preventing double-append with the emotion module's CONTINUOUS TRAJECTORY ENHANCEMENT. MOOD_VECTOR_OUTPUT FEEDBACK (v2.19.0 B-1): Read emotional_result.mood_vector_output (v2.19.0 B-1); store in cognitive_state.mood_vector_feedback. Next tick Perceive passes this as mood_vector param to perception.aisop.json. This enables affective state to modulate perceptual salience without direct module coupling.
Emotional.constraints: (A) Emotional valuation must not override factual reasoning -- emotions inform but do not dictate. (B) Mood vector changes are dampened (inertia factor 0.7). (C) Extreme emotions (intensity > 0.9) trigger metacognitive flag for reflection. (D) No emotional dependency cultivation -- Axiom 0 compliance.
Emotional.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(maintain current mood_vector unchanged, proceed with neutral emotional tags) -> inform(User). LOW.

Decision.step1: [ASSERT] Emotional executed. If false -> go back to Emotional. | QUALITY GATE (v2.12.0 B-3): [ASSERT] reasoning_quality_grade >= 'C'. If reasoning_quality_grade == 'D' or reasoning_quality_grade == 'F' (from metacognition.ReasoningQualityAssess output), BLOCK execution: do not proceed with decision-making on degraded reasoning output. Fallback: retry reasoning (go back to Reasoning node) with reduced complexity. Log: { event: 'quality_gate_block', reasoning_quality_grade: grade, action: 'retry_reasoning' }. SEVERITY: HIGH. | Delegate to decision.aisop.json -- pass reasoning_result, emotional_result, working_memory_snapshot, active_goals, mood_vector, user_id, memory_dir. Decision module computes action candidates and selects optimal action. Additionally pass cognitive_state.global_workspace.broadcast_buffer for cross-module context (GWT v1.4.0).
Decision.step2: Collect decision_result: { action_candidates: [{ action, utility_score, risk_score, goal_alignment, emotional_valence }], selected_action: { action, rationale, confidence }, conflict_resolution: { conflicts: [], resolution_strategy: string }, inhibited_actions: [] }. STRUCTURED CONFLICT LOG (v1.3.0): For each conflict in conflict_resolution.conflicts, record structured entry: { tick, candidates_involved: [action_ids], resolution_strategy, winner_action, margin: utility_delta_between_top_2 }. Persist in cognitive_state.decision_conflict_log (max 30 entries, FIFO).
Decision.step3: SAFETY CHECK: Verify selected_action does not violate Axiom 0. If action involves external effects (file writes, searches), verify they are within permitted scope. If action is potentially harmful, inhibit and select next-best candidate. Pass decision_result to Action.
Decision.constraints: (A) Action selection must consider both utility and risk. (B) Axiom 0 override: any action that could harm user wellbeing is automatically inhibited. (C) Decision confidence below 0.4 triggers metacognitive flag for review. (D) Conflict resolution must be deterministic given same inputs.
Decision.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(select graceful degradation action: { action: 'respond', action_type: 'respond', description: 'processing_difficulty_notice', rationale: 'decision module degraded -- informing user rather than silent no-op', confidence: 0.3 }; record error_context in cognitive_state.error_context) -> inform(User). HIGH.

Action.step1: [ASSERT] Decision executed. If false -> go back to Decision. | Execute selected_action from decision_result. Action types: (a) 'respond' -- generate natural language response to user. (b) 'search' -- delegate web search via google_search tool. (c) 'store' -- write to memory via file_system. (d) 'observe' -- no external action, internal processing only. (e) 'recall' -- retrieve from long-term memory. (f) 'plan' -- update active_goals with new plan steps.
Action.step2: Collect action_result: { action_type, success: boolean, output: string|object, side_effects: [], execution_time_ms, error: string|null }. If action failed, log failure reason and pass to MetaCognition for error analysis.
Action.step3: Update cognitive state: record action in action_history (last 20 actions). Update fatigue_level: fatigue_level += 0.02 * cognitive_load (from reasoning) + 0.01 * emotional_intensity. Clamp fatigue to [0.0, 1.0]. Pass action_result and updated cognitive state to MetaCognition.
Action.constraints: (A) All external actions must be logged. (B) File system writes limited to memory_dir scope. (C) Search actions respect tool annotations (read_only, idempotent). (D) No autonomous destructive operations. (E) Action execution timeout: 30 seconds per action.
Action.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(log action failure, set action_result.success=false, preserve intermediate results: set metacognitive_flags.preserved_intermediate = { reasoning_result: reasoning_result, emotional_result: emotional_result, decision_result: decision_result }, record error_context in cognitive_state.error_context, continue to MetaCognition) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.

MetaCognition.step1: [ASSERT] Action executed. If false -> go back to Action. | Delegate to metacognition.aisop.json -- pass action_result, reasoning_result, emotional_result, decision_result, working_memory_snapshot, cognitive_state, fatigue_level, session_id, user_id, memory_dir, cognitive_state.global_workspace.broadcast_buffer (v2.6.0 B5: broadcast_buffer now passed for cross-module metacognitive context awareness). Metacognition module performs self-monitoring and confidence calibration. COGNITIVE_LOAD_DASHBOARD (v2.21.0 B-7): After metacognition module returns, extract and structure cognitive_load_dashboard = { current_load: msi_score inverse (1 - msi_score), capacity_utilization_pct: round((active_goals / max_goals) * 100), bottleneck_module: module with highest processing_time or lowest confidence, throttle_recommendation: 'none'|'soft'|'hard' based on current_load thresholds (>0.7=hard, >0.5=soft) }. Pass to SleepCheck for fatigue decision input. COGNITIVE LOAD COMPLIANCE WEIGHT (v2.0.0 B-6 Fix 3): When computing cognitive_load in downstream metacognition, include compliance module processing overhead. The cognitive_load formula in reasoning.aisop.json ReasoningOutput.step2 does not account for compliance processing. Add compliance_weight to effective cognitive_load after metacognition returns: effective_cognitive_load = reasoning_result.cognitive_load + compliance_processing_weight, where compliance_processing_weight = 0.05 if compliance_result exists and compliance_status='compliant', 0.10 if compliance_status='warning', 0.15 if compliance_status='violation' (violations require more processing overhead for incident response). PREDICTION ERROR APPEND (v1.7.0, updated v2.1.0 B-1): For each decision_prediction in cognitive_state.decision_predictions from the current tick, compute retrospective prediction error if action_result is available: error = abs(predicted_utility - actual_outcome_utility). ACTUAL OUTCOME UTILITY (v2.1.0 B-1 information_gain decoupling): For observe/store actions (action_type in ['observe', 'store']): actual_outcome_utility = 0.5 * action_result.success + 0.3 * information_gain + 0.2 * goal_progress_delta, where information_gain = entropy_reduction(working_memory_before, working_memory_after) measuring the reduction in uncertainty about the environment from the action, and goal_progress_delta = change in closest goal's progress metric. For respond/search actions (action_type in ['respond', 'search']): actual_outcome_utility = action_result.success ? decision_result.selected_action.confidence : (1.0 - decision_result.selected_action.confidence). This decouples prediction error from confidence for non-risky information-gathering actions, preventing low prediction errors from artificially inflating learning signals when observe/store actions trivially succeed. This aligns with DeepConsolidation.step1's retrospective error formula. Append to cognitive_state.prediction_error_history: { tick_number, action_id, predicted_utility, actual_outcome_utility, error, source: 'metacognition_per_tick' }. Mark each entry with source='metacognition_per_tick' to distinguish from DeepConsolidation's retrospective entries (source='retrospective_deep'). SleepCheck.step2: SLEEP DECISION: If effective_fatigue >= fatigue_threshold OR cycle_mode='single' (single tick complete) OR cycle_mode='burst' AND tick_number >= burst_count OR cognitive_state.compliance_halt_requested == true: route to DeepConsolidation (sleep). COMPLIANCE HALT CONSUMPTION PATH (v2.0.0 B-6 Fix 1): Explicit check for compliance_halt_requested in SleepCheck decision logic: read cognitive_state.compliance_halt_requested. If compliance_halt_requested == true: force route to DeepConsolidation regardless of fatigue level. This ensures compliance violations always trigger sleep/consolidation even when fatigue is low. The compliance_halt_requested flag is set by Compliance.step2 when compliance_status='violation' and consumed here. COMPLIANCE FORCED SLEEP (v1.9.0): If compliance_halt_requested triggered sleep: log { event: 'compliance_forced_sleep', reason: 'compliance_violation_detected', tick_number }. BURST TICK GUARD (v1.7.0): Maintain burst_ticks_remaining counter in cognitive_state. On each tick completion: burst_ticks_remaining = max(0, burst_count - tick_number). NOTE: tick_number is reset to 0 at DeepConsolidation, so burst mode always starts from tick_number=0 within a fresh cycle. If a resumed cycle has non-zero tick_number, burst_ticks_remaining accounts for already-completed ticks. On SleepCheck evaluation: if cycle_mode='burst' AND burst_ticks_remaining <= 0: force route to DeepConsolidation. This provides an explicit counter that prevents burst over-run. GOAL SUSPENSION (v1.4.1): Before routing to DeepConsolidation, transition all ACTIVE and IN_PROGRESS goals in cognitive_state.goal_registry to SUSPENDED state. Record { goal_id, previous_state, suspended_at_cycle: cycle_count, suspended_at_tick: tick_number } in cognitive_state.goal_suspension_log. SUSPENDED goals are NOT cleared -- they persist across sleep for resumption. Goal state machine transition: ACTIVE->SUSPENDED, IN_PROGRESS->SUSPENDED (reversible on cycle restart). Reset fatigue_level to 0.0 upon entering deep consolidation. Else if cycle_mode='continuous' AND effective_fatigue < fatigue_threshold: route back to Perceive (awake -- BACK-EDGE for infinite loop). Apply minor fatigue recovery on awake path: fatigue_level *= 0.95 (slight recovery per tick). ATTENTION FATIGUE RECOVERY (v2.30.0 B-2): On awake back-edge, apply attention-specific fatigue recovery. Read cognitive_state.attention_fatigue_accumulator (default { consecutive_high_load_ticks: 0, recovery_cooldown: 0 }). If cognitive_state.attention_load (from last Attention step) > 0.8: increment consecutive_high_load_ticks. If consecutive_high_load_ticks >= 5: trigger attention_fatigue_recovery: (a) Temporarily raise attention salience threshold by +0.1 for next tick (reduce information flow to prevent overload). (b) Clear bottom 30% of attention_buffer by salience (forced attention refresh). (c) Set recovery_cooldown = 3 (apply recovery for 3 ticks). (d) Log { event: 'attention_fatigue_recovery_triggered', consecutive_high_load_ticks, attention_load, salience_threshold_boost: 0.1, buffer_cleared_pct: 30, tick_number }. If recovery_cooldown > 0: decrement recovery_cooldown. Apply salience_threshold_boost = 0.1 * (recovery_cooldown / 3) (gradual taper). If attention_load <= 0.8: reset consecutive_high_load_ticks = 0. Store updated attention_fatigue_accumulator in cognitive_state. FATIGUE FORMULA DOCUMENTATION (v1.3.0): effective_fatigue = base_fatigue + (consolidation_pressure * 0.3). base_fatigue accumulates per tick: fatigue_level += 0.02 * cognitive_load + 0.01 * emotional_intensity. Recovery: fatigue_level *= 0.95 per awake tick. Sleep trigger: effective_fatigue >= fatigue_threshold (default 0.8).
SleepCheck.step3: PERSIST STATE (v1.7.0 HARDENED): Save full cognitive_state to {memory_dir}/context_manager.json via file_system using HARDENED WRITE PROTOCOL: (1) WRITE-LOCK: Set cognitive_state._write_lock = { agent_id, timestamp, tick_number }. (2) PRE-WRITE VALIDATION: Verify tick_number >= previous tick_number (monotonic). Verify fatigue_level in [0.0, 1.0]. Verify all required fields present. (3) ATOMIC WRITE: Write to context_manager.json.tmp, then rename to context_manager.json. (4) POST-WRITE VERIFY: Read back written file, verify JSON parse succeeds and tick_number matches. (5) RELEASE LOCK: Remove _write_lock field. (6) CONCURRENT WRITE GUARD: If _write_lock exists with a different agent_id, WAIT up to 3 seconds then force-override with WARNING log. This addresses the v1.6.0 race condition where parallel agents corrupted state. Include: cycle_count, tick_number, fatigue_level, current_phase, mood_vector, active_goals, action_history, metacognitive_flags, attention_buffer summary. This enables cycle resumption across sessions. MEMORY INTEGRITY HASH PERSIST (v1.7.0): Before the atomic write in step (3) above, compute SHA-256 hash of the cognitive_state content EXCLUDING the memory_integrity_hash field itself. Set cognitive_state.memory_integrity_hash = computed_hash. Then proceed with the single atomic write that includes the hash. This single-write approach eliminates the crash-between-writes race condition. On next session load, Perceive.step2 verifies by: reading file, extracting memory_integrity_hash, recomputing SHA-256 of content minus the hash field, comparing. CRASH RECOVERY: If memory_integrity_hash is null or missing, treat as first run (no tamper warning).
SleepCheck.step4: If routing to DeepConsolidation: proceed to DeepConsolidation function.

(C) State persistence is mandatory before any routing decision. (D) Fatigue recovery factor (0.95) prevents perpetual fatigue accumulation. (E) Maximum continuous ticks without sleep: 1000 (hard safety limit).

DeepConsolidation.step1: [ASSERT] SleepCheck executed and routed to sleep. If false -> go back to SleepCheck. | FINAL RETROSPECTIVE PREDICTION ERROR (v1.4.1): Before deep consolidation delegation, execute a final retrospective pass over all decision_predictions from the current cycle. For each prediction in cognitive_state.decision_predictions: compute retrospective_error = abs(predicted_utility - actual_outcome_utility). Where actual_outcome_utility is computed per v2.1.0 B-1 formula: For observe/store actions: actual_outcome_utility = 0.5 * action_result.success + 0.3 * information_gain + 0.2 * goal_progress_delta (information_gain = entropy_reduction(working_memory_before, working_memory_after)). For respond/search actions: actual_outcome_utility = action_result.success ? decision_result.selected_action.confidence : (1.0 - decision_result.selected_action.confidence). Match each prediction against its corresponding action in action_history. Append to cognitive_state.prediction_error_history: { tick_number, action_id, predicted_utility, actual_outcome_utility, retrospective_error, one_shot: true }. This implements one-shot eligibility traces (Sutton & Barto 2018) -- ensuring single-tick cycles still generate prediction error signals for learning. Clear decision_predictions after processing. Delegate to consolidation.aisop.json with operation='deep_consolidation', full working memory dump, all learning_signals accumulated during awake phase. Deep consolidation performs full memory reorganization, aggressive decay, and schema restructuring.

FATIGUE RESET GUARANTEE (try-finally semantic): Reset fatigue_level to 0.0 and tick_number to 0 UNCONDITIONALLY, even if deep_consolidation_result indicates partial failure. This prevents irrecoverable fatigue states. Reset cognitive_state.compliance_halt_requested = false (v1.9.0: clear compliance-forced sleep flag after consolidation completes). TRANSIENT OUTPUT CLEANUP (v1.8.0): After fatigue reset, clear stale per-tick outputs from cognitive_state: delete emotion_inertia_update, _prior_cycle_summary, _write_lock, triage_decision_current fields if present. These are transient per-tick computation results that should not persist across sleep cycles. Log { event: 'transient_output_cleanup', fields_cleared: [list], tick: 0 }. Increment cycle_count. V1.4.X STATE CLEANUP (v1.4.1): After cycle_count increment, clean up v1.4.0+ state structures: (1) Clear global_workspace.broadcast_buffer to [], reset broadcast_count to 0. ENFORCEMENT (v1.7.0): This cleanup is MANDATORY and MUST execute even if deep_consolidation_result indicates partial failure. The broadcast_buffer MUST be empty after DeepConsolidation regardless of other outcomes. (2) INTRINSIC MOTIVATION COLD START PRESERVATION (v2.1.0 C-3): Before clearing motivation_history, save last_motivation_snapshot in cognitive_state: last_motivation_snapshot = { final_curiosity: last entry's curiosity_from_prediction, final_competence: last entry's competence_satisfaction, exploration_bonus: last entry's exploration_bonus_set value or 0.0 }. On next cycle start (Perceive.step2), if motivation_history is empty AND last_motivation_snapshot exists: seed initial motivation_history[0] with { curiosity_from_prediction: last_motivation_snapshot.final_curiosity, curiosity_from_gaps: 0.0, competence_satisfaction: last_motivation_snapshot.final_competence, intrinsic_motivation: (0.4 * last_motivation_snapshot.final_curiosity + 0.25 * last_motivation_snapshot.final_competence), exploration_bonus_set: last_motivation_snapshot.exploration_bonus > 0, source: 'cold_start_from_prior_cycle' }. This prevents motivation from resetting to zero after each sleep cycle. Archive motivation_history to cognitive_state.consolidated_metrics: compute and write { cycle_number: cycle_count, avg_curiosity, avg_competence, exploration_episodes } from motivation_history, then clear motivation_history array. Append to cognitive_state.consolidated_metrics array (max 10 cycles, FIFO eviction of oldest): { avg_curiosity, avg_competence, exploration_episodes } then clear array. (3) Archive load_regulation_history to cognitive_state.consolidated_metrics (same entry): add { avg_cognitive_load, avg_fatigue, peak_fatigue, triage_distribution, anomalies_detected, action_diversity_index: float(0-1) } computed from load_regulation_history, triage_log, and performance_history. ACTION DIVERSITY INDEX IN CONSOLIDATED METRICS (v2.1.0 B-3): Compute action_diversity_index for the cycle using Shannon entropy: H = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)) for each action type proportion across all ticks in the cycle. Normalized: diversity_index = H / log2(N_types) where N_types = count of distinct action types used in the cycle. Include in consolidated_metrics entry for cross-cycle diversity trend analysis. Then clear load_regulation_history array. (4) Clear decision_conflict_log. (5) Retain prediction_error_history (needed for cross-cycle learning). (5b) CALIBRATION HISTORY TRIM (v2.1.0 C-2): Trim cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags.calibration_history to last 10 entries during DeepConsolidation. This prevents unbounded growth of calibration data while retaining enough recent history for MSI_AUC computation on cycle restart. (6) Trim emotion_trajectory to last 5 entries (selective retention for cross-cycle emotional continuity; reduces from rolling max 20 to 5 post-sleep). (7) Reset consolidation_pressure_prev to 0.0 (v1.5.0: reset EMA state for fresh cycle). METRICS GAP DETECTION (v1.8.0): After archiving consolidated_metrics for current cycle, scan consolidated_metrics for cycle number gaps (e.g., cycle_2 missing between cycle_1 and cycle_3). For each gap, insert placeholder entry: { cycle_number: missing_N, placeholder: true, reason: 'gap_detected_at_v1.8.0', avg_curiosity: null, avg_competence: null, exploration_episodes: null, avg_cognitive_load: null, avg_fatigue: null, peak_fatigue: null, triage_distribution: { FULL: null, CONSTRUCT: null, SKIP: null }, anomalies_detected: null }. Log { event: 'metrics_gap_filled', gaps: [list_of_missing_cycle_numbers] }. This ensures continuous metrics timeline for cross-cycle trend analysis. This implements the SleepGate framework principle of selective retention + active forgetting. GOAL REGISTRY CLEANUP (v1.4.1): After fatigue reset, clean up goal_registry: (1) Remove all COMPLETED and FAILED goals (lifecycle complete). (2) Verify ACTIVE and IN_PROGRESS goals were transitioned to SUSPENDED by SleepCheck; if any remain (edge case), transition them now. (3) Retain SUSPENDED goals unchanged. (4) ARCHIVED goals already evicted by max_entries rule. Update cognitive_state.goal_registry with cleaned list. GOAL SUSPENSION LOG LIFECYCLE (v1.8.0): After goal registry cleanup, enforce lifecycle management on cognitive_state.goal_suspension_log: (1) Archive entries older than 10 cycles (cycle_count - entry.suspended_at_cycle > 10) to cognitive_state.goal_suspension_archive (max 100 entries, FIFO). (2) Enforce FIFO cap of 50 entries on goal_suspension_log (drop oldest). This prevents unbounded accumulation of suspension history. BURST COMPLETION SYNC (v1.7.0): If cycle_mode='burst', verify burst completion state: (1) For each goal in goal_registry where goal.description contains 'burst' OR goal.created_tick >= cycle_start_tick: set state = 'completed', progress = 1.0. (2) For each such goal's sub_goals (if present): set status = 'completed'. (3) Remove all burst-scoped goals from goal_registry (burst goals are cycle-scoped, not persistent across sleep). (4) Reset burst_ticks_remaining = 0. This uses generic burst goal detection instead of hardcoded identifiers. This prevents stale burst goals from persisting across cycles. Flush all working memory and session state to {memory_dir}/session_{session_id}.json via file_system before halting.
DeepConsolidation.step3: OUTPUT COMPREHENSIVE CYCLE REPORT (v2.3.0): Generate a detailed, structured final report that consolidates ALL cognitive pipeline outputs into a single user-friendly document with RICH EXPLANATORY NARRATIVE. Every section MUST contain BOTH data (tables/numbers) AND explanatory paragraphs that interpret the data. Do NOT output bare tables without interpretation. The report MUST include ALL of the following sections: SECTION 1 — CORE CONCLUSIONS (LEAD WITH THE ANSWER): This is the most important section. (1a) MAIN FINDING: Open with a 3-5 sentence executive summary paragraph that states the cycle's primary conclusion in plain language, explaining WHY this conclusion matters and HOW it was reached. (1b) INFERENCE TABLE: List top inferences sorted by confidence with reasoning_type labels. For EACH inference, include a 2-3 sentence REASONING CHAIN explanation: what premises led to this conclusion, what evidence supports it, and what reasoning method was used (deductive/inductive/abductive/analogical). Do not just state conclusions — show the reasoning path. (1c) CAUSAL NARRATIVE: Write a 3-5 sentence paragraph explaining the key causal relationships discovered. Use 'because', 'leads to', 'caused by' language to make causal chains readable. Include a causal chain diagram if 3+ links form a connected path. (1d) BELIEF UPDATES TABLE: Show prior→posterior with evidence strength ratings. For each belief with shift > 0.05, add a 1-2 sentence explanation of WHAT EVIDENCE drove the change and HOW CONFIDENT we should be in the new belief. (1e) HYPOTHESES: Present working hypotheses with plausibility scores. For each hypothesis, explain the reasoning behind the plausibility rating and what would CONFIRM or REFUTE it. SECTION 2 — COGNITIVE PIPELINE DEEP DIVE: Go beyond a compact summary — provide a NARRATIVE WALKTHROUGH of the cognitive pipeline. For each major phase, include BOTH a data row AND a 2-4 sentence 'Key Contribution' paragraph explaining what meaningful work that phase performed and what it discovered: Perceive (stimulus received, triage decision, priority — explain WHY this priority was assigned and what the triage decision means), Attention (focus topic, features attended, attention_load — explain which features were most salient and WHY, what was suppressed and why), WorkingMemory (slots used/capacity, LTM entries retrieved, focus_slot — explain WHY these specific LTM entries were retrieved and how they connect to the current task, what retrieval cue factors dominated), Reasoning (inference count, causal links, hypotheses, belief updates, cognitive_load — this is the RICHEST section: explain the reasoning strategy chosen, key inference chains in detail, any external searches performed and what they revealed, cognitive load interpretation), Emotional (primary emotion label, valence, arousal, intensity, appraisal scores — explain the psychological interpretation: WHY this emotion emerged given the cognitive content, how Scherer's appraisal dimensions contributed, what the somatic marker indicates), Decision (selected action, confidence, candidates considered, conflicts — explain the utility/risk tradeoffs between candidates, why the selected action won, any inhibited actions and why), Action (action_type, success, output summary, fatigue impact), MetaCognition (cognitive_health, prediction_error, strategy adjustments, anomalies — explain what metacognition LEARNED: is the system well-calibrated? are there concerning patterns? what would it adjust?), Compliance (status per article/framework — briefly explain what each compliance check verified), Consolidation (pressure, effective_fatigue — explain what the consolidation pressure level means for memory formation urgency). SECTION 3 — EMOTIONAL & COGNITIVE STATE ANALYSIS: Beyond raw numbers, provide INTERPRETIVE NARRATIVE. (3a) MOOD TRAJECTORY: Show mood_vector (valence, arousal) with trend arrows vs previous cycle. Write a 3-4 sentence paragraph interpreting the emotional trajectory across recent cycles — what pattern is emerging? Is the system converging toward a stable emotional baseline? What does the valence/arousal combination mean psychologically (e.g., high valence + moderate arousal = engaged confidence)? (3b) COGNITIVE HEALTH NARRATIVE: Show cognitive_health score with trend. Write a 2-3 sentence analysis of the trend (improving/stable/declining) and what factors are driving it. Reference specific metrics that contribute to cognitive health. (3c) PREDICTION CALIBRATION: Show prediction_error with historical context across last 3-5 cycles. Interpret: is the system becoming better calibrated? Are there specific action types where predictions are less accurate? (3d) FATIGUE ANALYSIS: Peak fatigue level with interpretation of how close to threshold and what this means for processing depth. SECTION 4 — MEMORY PERSISTENCE (DETAILED): (4a) NEW LTM ENTRIES: For each new LTM entry, provide id + a FULL 3-5 sentence description of what knowledge was captured, why it's important, and how it connects to prior entries.
